observations: The native body is a clear improvement: cap corners and visor have soft dimensional transitions, the fringe no longer cuts a sawtooth row through the cyan brim, ears/head/moustache read more softly, and sleeves/cuffs, collar, bib/pocket and apron belt are more intentional. Rowan remains recognizable in every actual facing.

Warm light tan skin, ginger hair/moustache, cyan cap, ivory coat, green apron, teal kerchief and dark shoes are retained. Broad smooth highlights show cap/head/clothing volume without hard directional cast shadows or dead black patches. Intended-size edges remain clean on light/gray/dark backgrounds.

All192 submitted indexed native frames were inspected through supplied four48-frame sheets, independent logical192x320 whole-frame scaling with a consistent diagnostic crop, representative raw frames and actual12fps playback. Forms and poses are stable; original small bob/work action/out-and-back load are retained. Repeated registration and neighbor/customer sprite assemblies show coherent character scale.

The exact canonical salmon appears clean and recognizable in S/E/W hold/load, with unchanged source palette/UV/width and original attachment motion. In N, the plate body is largely occluded but a bright white crescent remains exposed across the middle lower back of the head. It reads like a smile or plate embedded in the nape, rather than a coherent hidden prop. This is conspicuous at logical size, on every readability background, across all12 hold and12 load frames, and in the N belt assembly.

Original N evidence has a much thinner partial plate edge and a dark rectangular artifact. The new candidate removes that dark patch but makes the white crescent substantially larger and more legible as a false rear mouth. Preserving the old display constants does not remove the present visible defect. No additional body/lighting/style blocker was found.
